key_quotes: If EBITDA were to deteriorate materially from here, say below 1.8 billion on a trailing basis, then we would need to be having a different conversation. But that is not our base case. We are monitoring the situation closely and we have levers we can pull if needed.

I would say it is a matter of timing and optimising terms rather than access. We have had preliminary conversations with several banks and the reception has been constructive. We want to ensure we get the right structure and pricing. I would expect us to be in market within the next 60 to 90 days, subject to conditions.
If conditions deteriorate further, we have the flexibility to defer additional capex, but that would be a decision we hope not to have to make.
summary: Credit conditions show NO improvement from severely deteriorated Q4 2025 position. Leverage remains stuck at 5.8x with no deleveraging progress. Critical €1.8bn 2027 refinancing wall remains unaddressed 11 months later with management still 'exploring options' and repeating 60-90 day timelines. Covenant language frozen at 'adequate' with CFO explicitly 'monitoring closely' and repeating €1.8bn EBITDA floor warning. Defensive posture intensifies with management admitting 'flexibility to defer additional capex' if needed and asset sale proceeds 100% earmarked for debt reduction. Tone heavily hedged throughout with 'subject to', 'if conditions permit', 'we hope not to' - classic refinancing stress language at 908bps spreads with no concrete execution demonstrated.
